clue.text: Need to imprison individual, given bird for current transgressions?

indicators.note: to imprison something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to need something is to crave it
I, the single person speaking, stands for an individual
a mew is a gull, a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone longs to lock up a person and hand over a bird, as if listing the crimes of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to imprison' signals the container. The question mark flags that 'current' means present-day, not electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate of crimes happening at present is a wave of offences, so present-day lawbreaking fits with a punning question mark.

clue.text: "Punch" has old material

parts.note: to punch someone on the jaw is to chin them

explanation.surface: The satirical magazine Punch contains some old matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress 'Punch' up as the magazine; it is the verb meaning to hit on the jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twilled cotton cloth used for trousers, so it is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: First (which you have to be to win it), one takes nearly everything

parts.words: which you have to be to win it
parts.note: the lottery slogan says you have to be in it to win it, so these words point to the phrase in it
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: everything is all

explanation.surface: A competitor reflects that you have to enter to win, and that one winner scoops nearly the whole pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter of ALL, leaving AL. The bracket alludes to the UK National Lottery slogan 'You have to be in it to win it'.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial letter or stage is the first one, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: More subordinate to a 27?

definitions.meaning: additional, over and above what is usual
a minor background actor in a film ranks below the big name, the 27 entry

explanation.definitionFit: An extra is both something additional and a film walk-on, a bit player beneath any famous lead.

clue.text: Fitting a support, large fitting

parts.note: a prop is a support
OS, outsize, is a large clothing fitting or size

explanation.surface: Fitting a brace properly with a large fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'fitting' does two different jobs in the surface: the first is the definition, the second is a garment size.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means appropriate or pertinent, a synonym of fitting in the sense of suitable.

clue.text: Shift lies with spare trainers

indicators.note: to shift something is to move it around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shifts some untruths along with a pair of spare sports shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' rearranges LIES and SPARE. 'trainers' suggests sports shoes but means things that train plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Espaliers are trellises on which fruit trees are trained to grow flat, so they train the plants.

clue.text: Turn left for 18's work

parts.note: a bend is a turn
sinister is Latin and heraldic for left

explanation.surface: An instruction to go left as part of a writer's task.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is NABOKOV, whose 1947 novel has this title; in heraldry the term is a diagonal band running from the left.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of one of the Russian-American novelist's books, so it is an example of his output.

clue.text: Use stake to secure fine tangle

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a stake is a bet

indicators.note: a tangle mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone uses a post to hold down a fine knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in 'of some use'; 'tangle' and 'to secure' signal the anagram and container.
explanation.definitionFit: Benefit means advantage or use, as in 'of no benefit', a synonym of usefulness.

clue.text: Miners muse over conclusion of Thatcher, appearing superior figure

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it comes first

parts.note: the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers
Erato is the Muse of love poetry

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Striking miners brood over Margaret Thatcher's downfall as a powerful figure appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion of' takes R from Thatcher. The NUM was the British miners' union led by Arthur Scargill in the 1984-85 strike against Thatcher's government.
explanation.definitionFit: The numerator is the number written above the line in a fraction, so it is the upper figure.

clue.text: See 6
Old airline approaching a country

parts.note: Pan Am was a US airline that folded in 1991

explanation.surface: A defunct airliner comes in to land near a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a Central American nation, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: See books, then a work of 18

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
lit, short for literature, means books

explanation.surface: Look at books, then one novel by a certain author.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is NABOKOV, author of this 1955 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the Russian-American novelist's most famous book, so it is an example of his output.

clue.text: Post sack, work of 18

parts.note: a pale is a fence post or stake
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: Dismiss a mail sack as a writer's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is NABOKOV, author of this 1962 novel built around a long poem.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of one of the Russian-American novelist's books, so it is an example of his output.

clue.text: Man finally after scarf to get hot

indicators.note: after puts the final letter behind the scarf

parts.note: a stole is a long scarf

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A man puts on his scarf at last because he feels hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' looks like a temperature but is slang for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen, as in hot goods that the police are looking for.

clue.text: Pearl divers hit their target, primarily

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word
divers, meaning various, tells us the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Pearl divers reach their objective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is the old adjective meaning various, signalling the anagram of HIT THEIR; 'primarily' adds T from 'target'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pearl wedding anniversary marks thirty years of marriage, so pearl names that ordinal.

clue.text: Economy at first breaking no record is beginning to mint fresh coinage?

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes within
at first picks the opening letter

parts.note: a log is a record

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: With the economy in record-breaking form, the Royal Mint begins producing new coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts E inside NO. 'coinage' looks like money but means a newly coined word.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly invented word, and coining words is the idiom for inventing them.

clue.text: Watch muscle getting into condition

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

parts.note: a state is a condition
pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Watch a muscle get into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to watch as an onlooker, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Noble sailors in the wake of rotten stink

indicators.note: in the wake of means following behind, so the sailors come last

parts.note: high describes meat or game that has gone off
BO is body odour
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Aristocratic seamen follow a horrible smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Highborn means of noble birth, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Lover of 10, one hitching from Hull, perhaps, heading for Torquay

indicators.note: hitching means joining together, so the piece is coupled to a copy of itself

parts.note: Hull stands on the Humber estuary and was in the former county of Humberside

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker thumbs a lift from Hull bound for Torquay, the Devon seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' takes T from Torquay. 'hitching' doubles HUMBERT, the double-barrelled name of the narrator of LOLITA (10).
explanation.definitionFit: The narrator of the novel at 10 is infatuated with its young title character, so he is her lover.

clue.text: Writer brings to mouth very fine port

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something to the mouth lifts it up, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: OK means fine
Oban is a port on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A writer raises a glass of excellent port to his lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings to mouth' turns VOKOBAN upwards. 'port' looks like the wine but is the Scottish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was a Russian-American novelist, so he is an example of an author.

clue.text: Field where Kipling's Khan holds power

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside

parts.note: Shere Khan is the tiger in Kipling's The Jungle Book
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A field where the tiger in Kipling holds sway.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a field of activity or influence, as in sphere of expertise.

clue.text: See 17
Mass killer won't initiate search alongside a grave

parts.note: a tomb is a grave

indicators.note: something that won't initiate loses its first letter

parts.note: to comb is to search

explanation.surface: A mass murderer refuses to start hunting beside a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' reads as a church service or crowd, but the killer is a weapon; 'won't initiate' drops the first letter of the search word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear fission weapon kills on a huge scale, so it is a weapon of mass slaughter.

clue.text: Given a very meticulous leader, I'm backing plant

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Given a fussy boss, I am supporting the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole string ASOMIM round. 'plant' suggests a factory but is the flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a flowering shrub or tree, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Little thing that bites short dwarf

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: midget is an old word for a very small person

explanation.surface: A small biter is a little person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of MIDGET.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny biting fly, so it is a small insect that bites.

clue.text: Downright thin

definitions.meaning: utter or absolute, as in pure nonsense
very fine and see-through, as of fabric

explanation.definitionFit: Sheer means both utter, as in sheer folly, and diaphanous, as in sheer stockings.

clue.text: Enemy in action, one from Sana'a, perhaps

indicators.note: in action means moving around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An enemy fighter in combat, one from the Arab capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in action' rearranges ENEMY to YEMEN. Sana'a is the capital of Yemen, hence 'perhaps' for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sana'a is the capital of the Arabian country, so something from there is of that nation.

clue.text: Dish bound to pong, ending at the front

indicators.note: the ending at the front means the final letter is moved to the start

parts.note: an edge is a bound or boundary
pong is British slang for a stink, a reek

explanation.surface: A dish is sure to smell, with the end at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending at the front' moves the K of EDGEREEK to the start. Kedgeree is a British breakfast dish of rice, flaked fish and eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a cooked dish of rice, fish and eggs, so it is an example of a dish.

clue.text: Still go

definitions.meaning: a single photographic or film frame
an attempt, as in have a try

explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a photograph and also an attempt, as in have a shot at it.

clue.text: Great player has to fight in Balkan city

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Mostar is a city in Bosnia and Herzegovina
to vie is to compete or fight

explanation.surface: A great sportsman has to fight in a Bosnian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests a sportsman but means an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie star is a leading screen actor, and a player is an old word for an actor.
